questions.q: Why does LTV Global set the organization-wide default to Private on Account, Equipment Asset, Case, and Parts Order?
options: Because a more permissive default would require clawing back visibility after the fact across an enormous surface area, given the scenario's scale
Because Private is required by Salesforce for any org with more than 1,000 users
Because Private OWD disables sharing rules entirely
Because dealers cannot access Private records under any circumstances
questions.explain: Private is the conservative starting point this scenario's scale and complexity demand — every visibility exception becomes a deliberate grant instead of clawing back an accidentally permissive default.

questions.q: How does LTV Global's internal role hierarchy structure visibility across regions and business units?
options: Business unit first, then region, so a BU leader sees every region by default
There is no role hierarchy; all visibility comes from sharing rules alone
Region first, then business unit, so a regional leader sees everything in their region across business units without seeing other regions
Every role sits at the same level with no hierarchy at all
questions.explain: The hierarchy is structured region-first, then business unit, matching the vision's unified-customer-view commitment within a region while avoiding accidentally granting cross-region visibility by default.

questions.q: How do dealers and end customers access their own records under this design?
options: They are placed low in the internal role hierarchy so a manager above them can grant access
Through sharing sets tied to their own account relationship, entirely separate from the internal role hierarchy
They are given System Administrator profiles scoped to their own records only
They have no access to their own data and must call an internal rep for everything
questions.explain: Sharing sets grant external portal users access only to records matching their own account relationship, deliberately kept separate from the internal role hierarchy so one dealer can never be a hierarchy step away from another dealer's data.

questions.q: Why can a sales rep with full Account access still be unable to see a customer's credit score field?
options: Because credit score fields are stored outside Salesforce entirely
Because the sales rep's role is below the customer in the hierarchy
Because Account access always excludes all custom fields by default
Because field-level security is evaluated independently of object- and record-level access, and restricts that field to Equipment Financing profiles only
questions.explain: Field-level security operates independently of record-level access — a rep can have full Account visibility through the role hierarchy and still be blocked from a specific field like credit score, which is restricted to Equipment Financing profiles.

questions.q: How does this lesson resolve the open GDPR question left from Lesson 7, about EMEA not needing a separate org?
options: Through a combination of Private OWD, region-first role hierarchy, field-level security, Shield Platform Encryption, and (in Lesson 17) data-residency handling — no single mechanism alone
By stating GDPR does not apply to Salesforce implementations
By moving all EMEA data into LedgerPoint instead of Salesforce
By giving EMEA its own separate Salesforce org after all
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that no single mechanism satisfies GDPR alone — it's the combination of OWD, hierarchy, field-level security, encryption, and data-residency handling that makes the single-org decision defensible for EMEA.
